description: Locked analysis plan for benchmark_round3.py (mechanism of the high-load degradation, correlated patterns, multiplicity re-analysis of the round-2 cells, cache microbenchmark for the step above N^2, large complex128 timing). Committed with its lock BEFORE benchmark_round3.py exists or any round-3 experiment has been run; the git history shows the order.
author_knowledge_at_writing: Rounds 1 and 2 results are known (recall denoises at P/N <= 1/16, is worse than the cue at P/N >= 3/16, never beats a nearest-stored lookup; step above N^2 near 144 to 256 MiB working sets; reported L3 cache 320 MiB, L2 2 MiB per core, L1d 48 KiB per core on this VM). Also known before any round-3 data: (1) BPSK patterns are real, so the coupling matrix is real symmetric and the dynamics are synchronous +-1 Hopfield dynamics (verified numerically in the tests, not assumed); (2) classical cross-talk theory predicts a one-step bit error of Q(sqrt((N-1)/(P-1))) for an exact stored pattern with random patterns; (3) exactly orthogonal patterns (Hadamard rows) have zero cross-talk on an exact cue by algebra. No round-3 measurement existed when this file was written.

tests_for_multiplicity.statistic: paired per-trial gain (recall accuracy minus comparator accuracy); two-sided sign-flip permutation test of mean gain = 0 (assumes the gain distribution is symmetric about 0 under the null); p = (1 + #{|T*| >= |T_obs| - 1e-12}) / (1 + B); gains that are all exactly 0 give p = 1
tests_for_multiplicity.adjusted_verdict: denoises / degrades if the adjusted p < alpha and the mean gain is > 0 / < 0, otherwise inconclusive

families.round2_vs_cue: the 108 non-control bit-flip and phase-noise cells of the round-2 full profile, gain over the corrupted cue
families.round2_vs_nearest: the same 108 cells, recall minus nearest-stored-pattern accuracy
families.correlated_vs_cue: all cells with q > 0 in the correlated-pattern experiment
families.mechanism_t25: random-pattern cells with q > 0 in the mechanism experiment, gain at step 25

round2_reanalysis.method: rerun the round-2 full denoising profile with the same seed and per-trial output (benchmark_round2.bench_denoising with trial_sink; output unchanged); verify every cell reproduces results/round2/full_run1.json (recall, cue, nearest accuracy, gain, CI) exactly after rounding; then compute sign-flip p-values and Holm / BH adjusted verdicts. Report how many raw verdicts survive and which change. If the stored cells do not reproduce, report that as a failure.

mechanism.question: WHY does recall become worse than the cue at high load?
mechanism.recall_dynamics: s <- exp(i*angle(W s)) repeated, W from HolographicMemory.finalize() (zero diagonal), identical to HolographicMemory.recall; trajectories are recorded for 100 steps (bits at every step) and checked equal to mem.recall(steps=t) at t = 25.
mechanism.hadamard_note: P distinct rows drawn at random from rows 1..N-1 of the Sylvester Hadamard matrix of order N (exactly orthogonal, zero row sum); target = first drawn row; used as a zero-cross-talk causal control

classification.distance: normalised Hamming distance d_mu between the final bit vector (step 100) and each stored pattern; the negated pattern has distance 1 - d_mu

categories.retrieved_other_stored: d_0 > tau and min_{mu != 0} d_mu <= tau
categories.mirror_target: 1 - d_0 <= tau (final state is the negated target)
categories.mirror_other: 1 - d_mu <= tau for some mu != 0 and not mirror_target
categories.spurious: d_mu > tau and 1 - d_mu > tau for every stored mu (not near any stored pattern or its negation)

classification.precedence: retrieved_target, retrieved_other_stored, mirror_target, mirror_other, spurious (first match; ties cannot occur for tau < 0.25)
classification.dynamics_classes: fixed point if bits at steps 98, 99, 100 are identical; period-2 cycle if bits(100) == bits(98) != bits(99); otherwise still moving. convergence step = first t <= 100 with bits(t) == bits(t-1), or 'not converged'.

mechanism.x_cells: the random-pattern cells with q > 0 whose gain over the cue at step 25 is 'degrades' after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment (family mechanism_t25); hypothesis verdicts below pool trials over these cells. If there are fewer than 3 x-cells every hypothesis is reported 'not testable'.

a_crosstalk.claim: interference (cross-talk) from the other stored patterns causes the degradation
a_crosstalk.a1_test: random patterns, q = 0: measured one-step error e1 = 1 - bit accuracy at step 1 versus the Gaussian cross-talk prediction Q(sqrt((N-1)/(P-1))). Testable cells: predicted error count over trials*N bits >= 5. A cell agrees if the prediction lies inside the 95% bootstrap CI of e1 or the ratio measured/predicted is within [1/1.5, 1.5].
a_crosstalk.a2_test: orthogonal control: in the Hadamard kind the q = 0 one-step error must be exactly 0 (harness check, reported as a failure otherwise). For each x-cell, take the Hadamard cell with the same N, P/N, q and test its gain at step 25 the same way.
a_crosstalk.supports: a1: >= 75% of testable cells agree and there are >= 3 testable cells; AND a2: in >= 80% of x-cells the Hadamard cell is NOT 'degrades' (BH-adjusted) and the mean final (step 25) accuracy of the Hadamard cells exceeds the random cells by >= 0.05
a_crosstalk.rejects: in >= 50% of x-cells the Hadamard cell is also 'degrades', or a1 fails in more than half of testable cells

b_spurious.claim: recall converges to spurious states (not near any stored pattern or its negation)
b_spurious.measure: pooled fraction of x-cell trials classified 'spurious' at step 100, tau = 0.10, with a Wilson 95% CI
b_spurious.sensitivity: same pooled fraction at tau in {0.02, 0.05, 0.20}

c_mirror.claim: recall converges to the negated stored pattern (global sign mirror)
c_mirror.measure: pooled fraction of x-cell trials classified 'mirror_target' or 'mirror_other' at step 100, tau = 0.10, Wilson 95% CI

d_dynamics.claim: the 25-step recall is truncated, still moving, or oscillating
d_dynamics.measures: pooled over x-cells: mean accuracy at step 100 minus step 25 with a bootstrap CI; fraction of trials with bits(25) != bits(100); fraction period-2 at step 100 (Wilson); number of x-cells whose step-100 gain over the cue is no longer 'degrades' (BH-adjusted, family recomputed for step 100)
d_dynamics.supports_truncation: |mean accuracy change 25 -> 100| >= 0.02 AND fraction of trials with bits(25) != bits(100) >= 0.25
d_dynamics.rejects_truncation: |mean accuracy change| < 0.01 AND fraction changed <= 0.10 (the degradation is a converged property, not a transient)
d_dynamics.supports_oscillation: pooled period-2 fraction at step 100 has Wilson lower bound >= 0.10

correlated.question: How do the capacity (exact-cue accuracy) and the denoising verdicts change when stored patterns are correlated?
correlated.generator: common +-1 pattern c; each pattern bit equals c_i with probability (1 + sqrt(rho))/2, independently across patterns and bits. Marginals are uniform and the expected pairwise correlation between any two patterns is exactly rho. rho = 0 is plain random patterns with new seeds (an independent replication of round 2 for q = 0.1 and 0.3).
correlated.endpoints: q = 0: recall bit accuracy with bootstrap CI, exact-recall fraction with Wilson CI, knee = smallest tested P/N with mean accuracy < 0.95 (as in round 1). q > 0: gain over the cue (paired bootstrap CI; raw verdict D/X/~; BH and Holm adjusted verdicts in the family correlated_vs_cue), gain versus nearest-stored (matched filter), realised mean pattern overlap.

hypothesis_e.claim: correlation shrinks the region where recall denoises
hypothesis_e.measure: number of cells with BH-adjusted verdict 'denoises' per rho (36 cells per rho: 3 values of N x 6 values of P/N x 2 values of q > 0)

correlated.replication_check: for rho = 0, q in {0.1, 0.3} (36 cells) report how many raw verdicts equal the round-2 verdicts for the same N, P/N, q; differences are reported, not hidden.

cache_microbenchmark.question: Is the step above N^2 (matvec time per byte jumps up near working sets of 144 to 256 MiB) explained by cache or memory bandwidth?
cache_microbenchmark.cache_info: parsed from /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache/index* and lscpu: level, type, size, shared_cpu_list. Caches reported here are those of a KVM guest; the real share of the L3 available to this guest is unknown.

matvec.operation: w @ s for a dense N x N matrix, dtype complex128 and complex64; one sample = k matvecs where k = ceil(0.005 s / time of one matvec), per-op time = sample / k
matvec.memory_rule: peak = matrix bytes + 64 MiB; measure only if peak <= 4 GiB and <= 0.5 * MemAvailable at the time of the check
matvec.metric: effective matrix read bandwidth = matrix bytes / per-op time (GB/s); local log-log slope of time versus N

streaming_read.operation: numpy sum of a contiguous float64 array (single thread), bandwidth = array bytes / time
streaming_read.sizes_bytes: geomspace from 16 KiB to 1 GiB, 49 points, each rounded to a multiple of 4096 bytes

cache_microbenchmark.drop_event: adjacent sizes in the measured series where the bandwidth falls to <= 0.75 of the previous point; boundary working set B = the two sizes that bracket it

m1_reported_cache.claim: the matvec bandwidth drop coincides with a reported cache capacity
m1_reported_cache.supports: a matvec drop event (complex128, one thread) has its bracketing working sets W_lo <= C <= W_hi for some reported cache size C (per-core L1d, per-core L2, total L3)
m1_reported_cache.rejects: the matvec drop events exist but none brackets a reported cache size
m1_reported_cache.otherwise: inconclusive (no drop event, or too few points)

m2_streaming_drop.claim: the matvec bandwidth drop coincides with a drop in plain single-thread streaming read bandwidth, whatever the reported cache sizes
m2_streaming_drop.supports: the bracket [W_lo, W_hi] of the complex128 one-thread matvec drop overlaps the bracket of a streaming-read drop event
m2_streaming_drop.rejects: the streaming-read curve has no drop event overlapping the matvec drop

hypotheses.reading_rule: A match is reported as 'consistent with', never as proof of mechanism; page-table (TLB) and hypervisor effects are not separated by this microbenchmark and are listed as untested alternatives.

complex128_large.question: Can complex128 be timed directly at a size close to 16384 without exceeding 4 GiB?
complex128_large.implementation: benchmark_round3.py only: complex128 coupling matrix (16 N^2 bytes) built in 64 MiB row chunks from 8 random BPSK patterns (diagonal zeroed), recall loop identical to HolographicMemory.recall in complex128. Dense matvec time does not depend on the matrix values.
complex128_large.memory_rule: peak <= 4 GiB AND peak <= 0.5 * MemAvailable; if the rule fails, poll every 30 s for up to 300 s and recheck before recording measured=false with the reason
complex128_large.cross_check: N = 8192 is timed with this implementation so it can be compared with the HolographicMemory timing of round 2 (one thread 2.30 s, default threads 0.30 to 0.32 s)
complex128_large.extrapolation: log-log fit on the load-controlled measured sizes of this list (>= 3 points); extrapolated to 16384 and labelled EXTRAPOLATED, NOT MEASURED, interval = bootstrap of per-N medians; compare with the original claim 2.2 to 3.5 s

determinism.hash_scope: protocol hash, profile, seed, mechanism results, correlated-pattern results, multiplicity re-analysis (including permutation p-values), and the timing plans; excludes every timing, load measurement, memory-availability decision, cache information and everything derived from them
determinism.ci: quick mode is run twice in CI and the deterministic_sha256 lines are diffed; full mode is manual only

must_report: every hypothesis with its pre-declared verdict word (supported / rejected / partial-inconclusive / not testable) and the numbers behind it
whether the round-2 stored cells reproduced
the cache result as 'consistent with' or 'inconclusive'
reporting.wording: synthetic classical software; no quantum-hardware, QEC or quantum-advantage claim; timings are for this machine and this load
